milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Requires MCP stdio credential injection to pass through a Runtime-owned secret reference contract without widening Mode Pack policy or tool authority.
Allows autonomous runs to use trusted MCP servers that require scoped credentials while preserving replay-safe bounded evidence and fail-closed launch semantics.
Keeps MCP tool execution request-scoped and environment-cleared while permitting only explicitly configured secret references resolved at launch.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement, headless_autonomous_development, and controlled_workspace_tools by adding a bounded Runtime-owned secret reference launch path for MCP stdio servers.
answers.new_capability: Trusted Mode Pack MCP server config can name bounded secret references that Runtime resolves and injects only into the request-scoped tools/list or tools/call child environment.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before MCP-S6, Brownie correctly cleared inherited environment, but there was no auditable path for intentionally supplying scoped credentials to trusted MCP stdio servers without raw environment values.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Credentialed MCP servers would either remain unusable or pressure callers toward unsafe raw environment inheritance, raw Mode Pack secrets, or external wrapper behavior outside Runtime evidence.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes Mode Pack MCP config admission, Runtime stdio launch behavior, catalog provenance, execution metadata, specs, and audits; it is not a wrapper, adapter manifest, hosted secret manager, or documentation-only verdict.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tools/list, tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume boundaries are preserved; secret resolution is Runtime launch plumbing below those surfaces.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase updates existing execution behavior and bounded evidence rather than adding a report, readiness endpoint, or diagnostic wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Raw MCP env values fail closed at Mode Pack validation, unresolved references fail before spawn, and successful launches inject only resolved scoped values after env_clear while evidence exposes only fingerprints/counts.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless runs can execute authorized credentialed MCP stdio tools without inheriting ambient secrets or replaying raw secret material; resume relies on bounded completed evidence rather than persisted secret values.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes MCP-S6 and leaves MCP-S7 executable identity as the remaining MCP safety phase before the campaign can move past stdio MCP safety closure.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S6 changes Runtime MCP stdio launch behavior and Runtime release audit state, so strict review must verify secret references remain launch-scoped, fail closed, and never persist raw secrets or widen authority.

exit_criteria: Trusted Mode Pack MCP server config accepts only bounded structured env secret_ref bindings.
Raw environment values, unsupported binding shapes, malformed names, duplicate secret references, oversized references, and unresolvable references fail closed.
Runtime resolves secret references only through a Runtime-owned resolver immediately before request-scoped tools/list and tools/call stdio launch.
The MCP child environment remains cleared except for deterministic Runtime values and explicitly resolved scoped secret bindings.
Raw secret values and raw environment maps are not persisted, returned, prompt-materialized, ledgered, or recorded in control-plane documents.
Secret references cannot override Mode Pack allow-lists, mcp_tool_access, S2 safety policy, S3 annotations, S4 approval binding, S5 schema validation, catalog drift, or Runtime authority.
MCP-S6 is marked closed while MCP-S7 and Runtime Release Ready remain open.
behavior_evidence: brownie-modepack focused test coverage proves valid structured secret references compile and raw or duplicate MCP env bindings fail closed.
brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves secret references are injected into request-scoped child environments without result exposure and unresolved references fail before spawn.
docs/architecture/mcp-runtime-safety-policy-audit.json records MCP-S6 as closed while leaving MCP-S7 open.

accepted_capability: MCP stdio secret references are Runtime-resolved, request-scoped, and bounded.
Credentialed MCP launch remains task-pinned, provenance-bound, environment-cleared, and replay-safe without raw secret persistence.
behavior_evidence: Runtime and Mode Pack focused test coverage proves accepted structured references, raw value rejection, duplicate-reference rejection, launch-time injection, unresolved pre-spawn failure, and bounded evidence.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
Mode Pack structured policy remains the MCP tool safety authority; MCP secret references, schemas, annotations, descriptions, results, and model output cannot grant authority.

Secret references only resolve scoped child environment values at launch; they cannot widen Mode Pack policy, allow-list membership, approval binding, annotations, schema validation, or catalog provenance.
non_goals: Does not add a hosted secret manager, Vault, KMS, OAuth, Streamable HTTP, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, registry, or automatic install.
Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.
Does not add scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, recursive Brownie invocation, or remote Git expansion.
Does not close MCP-S7 executable identity.
Does not close full CI workflow hardening while workflow update authority is unavailable.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected raw env strings in Mode Pack config because credential values must not become policy data or persisted evidence.
Rejected ambient environment inheritance because MCP-S1 through MCP-S5 safety assumes stdio children do not inherit arbitrary Runtime/user shell state.
Rejected CLI-owned or provider-owned secret resolution because Runtime owns MCP launch, evidence, replay, and permission boundaries.
Rejected hosted secret-manager integration because MCP-S6 only defines the minimal resolver contract required for local stdio release safety.
technical_debt: Previously recorded Runtime Release Readiness blockers remain open, including full CI workflow hardening.

runtime_release_dod: Runtime-owned MCP permission checks, tool execution, bounded evidence, replay, completion semantics, and request-scoped stdio launch.
Task-pinned Mode Pack policy, catalog provenance, annotation provenance, approval provenance, schema provenance, secret reference fingerprints, and point-of-use Runtime safety enforcement.
runtime_boundary_contracts: Existing tool.execute, task.run, tools/list, tools/call, and headless run/resume paths.
Existing ToolExecutionCompleted, ToolExecutionFailed, ToolExecutionDenied, MCP catalog, schema validation, and approval ledger evidence.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduling, background polling, daemonization, hosted queues, worker fleets, and remote server operations.
external_adapter_responsibilities: MCP server implementation, GitHub/GitLab/Slack adapters, OAuth application wiring, remote transport hosting, and hosted credential management.
commercial_solution_readiness: Enterprise tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin UI, monitoring backend, billing, SLA, private registry, and certified stack.

next_capability_rationale: MCP-S7 should add MCP server executable identity evidence and drift checks before tools/list and tools/call without ledgering raw paths or binary content.
